title: Boot path and kernel init
summary: The boot path is one of the best-reasoned parts of the tree. Stage 1 relocates itself by arithmetic and checksums the 13-sector stage 2 it reads. Stage 2 reads a whole cylinder per int 13h call and checks the transfer rather than the table. kmain's boot half runs from that blob, which is given back to the heap floor and compacted away, so boot-only code costs no resident byte. That beats what DOS, Windows 3.x or System 6 did with init code. But the guard whose whole purpose is the fault no emulator reproduces is defeated on four of the six shipped system disks. Since kernel size pass 14 took BOOT2_SECS from 12 to 13, stage 2's first run on kern_big's 360KB and 720KB images starts on head 1 and never crosses a head, and the canary (file sector 21) sits in that run. On the BIOS it exists for it passes, publishes boot_cylrun and lets dsk_xfer write across heads all session. t_canary stayed green because it models runs from the data area, not from data+BOOT2_SECS. The fix is two numbers (file sector 57). On kern_small's 360KB and 720KB disks and on kern_big's 1.2MB disk the canary sector is placed correctly, but the splash's first tick executes vid_setmode/gfx_rowbase out of sectors loaded past the first head crossing, before the canary runs, so on that BIOS the machine runs garbage before it can be rescued (boot-2, verified worse than first reported). The rest is the usual shape of a heavily size-passed area. A guard label sits four bytes short of the stores it is meant to cover, while the rung it guards is four sectors too big. The second loader (boothd) still asks a RAM question boot.asm retired, and the kernel fetches the boot partition's BPB with the int 13h AH=08h geometry the hard-disk sector deliberately stopped trusting. Stage 2 keeps a dead duplicate of the DPT patch in a blob with 4 bytes free. Guard 5 omits BLOB_LIFT on every shipped kernel (ROM_COLD is the default, not a knob). And more than forty comments and SPEC passages state wrong current values because they narrate history instead of invariants. Nothing here needs an ABI break.

strengths.title: The boot blob sits at the heap FLOOR and is given back and compacted
strengths.why: Every boot-only body (the loader, the splash, kmain_o, two dozen *_x init routines) is in .boot2 and rejoins the long free run at the bottom of the heap. A transient at the top would strand itself above unmovable claims. This is the model any new boot-only code should follow, and it beats DOS's SYSINIT, which in practice was lost memory.

strengths.title: Verify the TRANSFER, never the table
strengths.why: Reading back your own int 1Eh patch proves nothing; summing a sector that a crossing run delivered does. Using the sum rather than the first word closed the kern_mega case where the wrong sector's first word was also 0. The principle is right even though the sector is currently in the wrong place (boot-1).

strengths.title: Stage 1 checksums stage 2
strengths.why: It catches the failure that is not a disk error (a sector that silently did not arrive) for a 20 ms loop. BOOTDIAG=1 prints the sum, so the missing sector can be named from the host.

strengths.title: Assembly-time arithmetic instead of dead runtime checks
strengths.evidence: boot.asm 137-147 (MEMNEED clamp); boot2.asm 515-519 (packed-tail vs blob); kernel.asm 8873 (.cfx vs BLOB_SEG_AT); boot2.asm 883
strengths.why: Each one turns a field fault into a build failure at zero bytes.

strengths.title: A range check on DL rather than a fallback
strengths.why: A range check cannot load a kernel off the wrong disk; a fallback can. The reasoning is written at the site.

strengths.title: Fixed low words with a registry indirection
strengths.why: A cheap, ABI-stable channel between the loader, the kernel and the test harness. The registry means the next instrument does not need a word of its own.

strengths.title: One decoder serves both loaders
strengths.why: The hard disk and the floppy place the packed tail at the same address because their arithmetic agrees, so the HDD door is a short move plus the floppy's own kz_all, with no second copy to drift.

strengths.title: The interrupt has its own far pointer
strengths.why: spl_ifp exists because SPLCALL stages its target in a shared word two instructions before the call. A one-boot-in-fifty race was closed by construction rather than by cli.

strengths.title: Section-end guards for every section
strengths.why: A stray section switch cannot silently under-report a size that a ladder rung is derived from.

strengths.title: boothd's CHS proof on bytes read off a disk
strengths.why: The two guards that make a single div pair safe against a hostile BPB are written beside the failure each prevents: an INT 0 into POST's vector, or a cylinder-1024 wrap that jumps into the wrong sectors.

strengths.title: cpu_detect's x87 scratch word on its own stack frame
strengths.why: The deliberate no-override [bp+0] encoding is documented as the mechanism, together with why a 'fix' would break 8087 detection. That is how a non-obvious encoding should be documented.

findings.title: The boot canary is inert on kern_big's 360KB and 720KB disks, and t_canary cannot see it
findings.detail: Stage 2 starts reading at data+BOOT2_SECS. On kern_big's 360KB and 720KB images the data area is LBA 14 (fatsz 3), so .text begins at LBA 27, which is cylinder 1, head 1, sector 1. read_run bounds runs at the cylinder, so run 1 is LBA 27..35, on head 1 only, and crosses no head. KSIG_OFF 4096 is kernel sector 8 = file sector 21 = LBA 35, inside that run. On a BIOS that flips heads at the wrong sector (the canary's whole reason; on a 286 this is reachable once the user ticks Cylinder), every later cylinder's head-1 half loads wrong and the canary still passes. Stage 2 then publishes [0060:0004], dsk_cylrun becomes 1, and every multi-sector WRITE for the session crosses heads on that BIOS. kernel size pass 14 (BOOT2_SECS 12 -> 13) broke it: at 12, .text began on head 0 sector 9 and run 1 crossed. t_canary's crosses() walks runs from the data area instead of from data+BOOT2_SECS, so it reports file sector 21 as crossing. Under the real partition, the legal band over all six shipped system images and the 11/13/14-sector blob lengths is {57, 106..110}. The 1.2MB and 1.44MB disks and both kern_small disks are correct today (but see boot-2 for kern_small and 1.2MB).
evidence: build/os8088-360.img and os8088-720.img BPB: rsvd 1, nfat 2, fatsz 3, root 112 -> data at LBA 14
boot/boot2.asm:467 publishes the bound; kernel/disk.inc:5343-5346 dsk_cylrun
findings.recommendation: Move the canary to file sector 57: KSIG_OFF := 22528 in the Makefile, and KSIG_OFF equ 22528 - BOOT2_KNOBSEC*512 + BOOT2_SMALLSEC*512 in boot2.asm (memory sector 44 on kern_big, 46 on kern_small, both inside .text; under KZIP it falls in the packed tail, which the existing %if arm handles). Fix t_canary's crosses() to start each walk at data + boot2_secs (and its docstring with it), then break it on purpose (KSIG_OFF back to 4096) and watch os8088-360.img go red. Better still, see boot-10.
findings.verify_note: Re-derived from the built images' BPBs: 360/720 data LBA 14, spt 9, heads 2; .text at LBA 27 = cyl 1 h1 s1; run 27..35 single-head; canary LBA 35 inside it. A walk from data+BOOT2_SECS gives ok(21)=False for blob 13 and 14 on both 9/2 disks and True on 1.2MB, 1.44MB and both small disks; the intersection is [57,106,107,108,109,110]. t_canary.crosses() really starts at lba = data. Not listed in ABI-BREAK-LIST or KERNEL-BYTE-QUEUE.

findings.title: The splash runs code from crossing runs before the canary has verified them, which defeats the canary on kern_small's floppies and kern_big's 1.2MB
findings.detail: After every run, stage 2 ticks spl_tick once SPL_RESIDENT sectors are aboard. The first tick far-calls vid_setmode and gfx_rowbase (kern_big .text 0x7F5 / 0x8C4, sectors 3 and 4; kern_small 0x766 / 0x7E4, both sector 3), and spl_isr keeps calling gfx_rowbase from IRQ0. The canary only runs after the whole load. On kern_small's 360KB and 720KB disks (the 128KB XT's own, data at LBA 12, blob 11) .text starts at LBA 23 = head 0 sector 6, run 1 is LBA 23..35 and crosses at .text sector 4; on the EOT-8 BIOS the canary exists for, the wrong delivery already starts at .text sector 3 (head 0 sector 9), which holds both routines. On kern_big's 1.2MB disk .text starts at LBA 42 (head 0 sector 13) and run 1 crosses at kernel sector 3. In both cases the machine executes garbage at the first tick, before the shorten-and-reload can run, so the canary - correctly placed on those disks - never gets to rescue the boot. The KZIP plain head is read with the same bound. kern_big's 360KB/720KB (run 1 head-1 only) and 1.44MB (first crossing at .text sector 8) are not exposed.
evidence: build/small360.img / small720.img BPB: data LBA 12, spt 9, heads 2
findings.recommendation: Keep the TRACK bound until the resident head is aboard: widen b2_runmax to the cylinder only once SPL_RESIDENT sectors have landed (move the mul at 306-310 behind a [b2_left] test). This costs one extra int 13h on geometries whose first head crossing falls inside the head (kern_small 360/720 and kern_big 1.2MB today). Verifying the canary before the first tick instead would delay the bar to about a third of the load once boot-1 moves the canary to sector 44.
findings.bytes_est: +8 blob (.boot2, transient); needs boot-7's room on kern_big
findings.verify_note: Mechanism confirmed. Corrected exposure and severity (medium -> high): the reviewer said 360/720 are not exposed, which holds only for kern_big; kern_small's 360KB and 720KB disks (the 128KB XT target, i.e. the machines most likely to carry an EOT-8 clone BIOS) are exposed, because their .text starts at head 0 sector 6 and vid_setmode/gfx_rowbase sit in .text sector 3. On those disks this, not boot-1, is what defeats the canary.

findings.title: A canary reload resets the splash's .text state while the blob still thinks the splash is up
findings.detail: .rerun reloads from .text sector 0. That re-lands spl_live, spl_busy and spl_quiet (.text 0x922-0x925) and the vid_* block (0x753-0x795) with their image defaults. [cs:spl_on] lives in the blob and stays 1, so the second pass's spl_tick skips the first-tick branch and never raises spl_live again. The consequences: spl_isr refuses every frame; spl_paint draws the bar with the default vid_* values (the wrong segment on CGA or Hercules); vid_init sees spl_live = 0 and performs the mode set the splash was protecting, which wipes the screen; and every later spl_step takes the 'finished' exit. The loading screen is gone for the rest of the boot, on exactly the machines the reload rescues.
findings.recommendation: Test the kernel byte for the first-tick branch: cmp byte [spl_live],0 / jne .running in place of cmp byte [cs:spl_on],0, keeping the mov byte [cs:spl_on],1 that spl_step needs. After a reload, the next tick re-probes, re-draws the chrome and re-raises spl_live. spl_hook is already guarded by spl_hooked.
findings.verify_note: Main claim confirmed (spl_on is a blob byte at .boot2 1585; spl_live and the vid_* block are .text sector 3/4 bytes the reload re-lands). The reviewer's secondary claim - that the DMA zeroing spl_busy under an in-flight spl_isr frame lets a nested IRQ0 start a second frame - is refuted and removed: the DMA writes ascending, so spl_live (0x922) is already 0 when spl_busy (0x924) is, and a nested spl_isr refuses at its spl_live test first.

findings.title: The SPL_RESIDENT guard stops four bytes short of the stores it is meant to cover, and the rung is four sectors too big
findings.detail: SPL_RES_SIZE is measured at spw_resident_end. The first tick writes spl_live and spl_busy and reads spl_quiet, all placed after that label. SPEC 2.9.4's own rule is that 'a first-tick store belongs in the head or in the blob', and the guard does not check it. Meanwhile SPL_RESIDENT is 9 against a measured need of 0x926 = 2,342 bytes (5 sectors) on kern_big and 0x846 on kern_small, and viddet.inc's comment claims sector 7. Under KZIP, KZ_HEADSEC equals SPL_RESIDENT, so 4,608 bytes of .text ship unpacked where 2,560 would do. The guard's own %error text also still says to raise SPL_RESIDENT 'in BOTH kernel/splash.inc and boot/boot2.asm'; boot2.asm defines none.
findings.recommendation: (a) Move spw_resident_end below spl_quiet (0 bytes). (b) Derive SPL_RESIDENT as (SPL_RES_SIZE+511)/512 at the foot of kernel.asm and have the Makefile read it from the ks: %warning line instead of sed-ing splash.inc; SPL_RESIDENT only reaches .boot2 immediates and KZ_HEAD, which the existing two-pass KZIP build already sequences. Before lowering it, audit every store the first tick can make (vid_setmode, vid_wipe, vid_cga_equip, vid_6845_prog, bvs_apply) for an address in sectors 5-8. (c) Correct the %error string (a code change, so it is not in doc_fixes).
findings.bytes_est: 0 resident; ~-400 bytes of KERNEL.SYS on kern_big (2,048 more bytes packed at ~80%)
findings.verify_note: Facts confirmed against both maps and kernel.kz.json (73904/92082 = 80.3%, so ~400 bytes saved). Severity lowered medium -> low: the uncovered stores are 4 bytes and today sit 1,770 bytes below the guarded boundary, so the gap can only bite if the label lands within 4 bytes of a sector end; the size win is disk, not RAM.

findings.title: A hard-disk boot fetches its own BPB with the AH=08h geometry that boothd deliberately stopped trusting
findings.detail: boothd reads with the BPB's spt and heads, because the geometry that wrote the volume is the only one that reads it back (FIELD-NOTES 33). The kernel's dsk_boot_from_x instead asks int 13h AH=08h, and dsk_bpb_check's first read of the boot partition (the read that fetches the BPB, converting bpb_hidd into CHS) uses that answer. Where the two differ, boothd boots and the kernel then fails to mount its own boot volume: no SYSTEM.CFG, no HDD.DRV, and a desktop that looks like it works. The comment at the AH=08h call still says it is 'the same question boot/boothd.asm asks'.
findings.recommendation: Hand the geometry over: boothd sets SI=[spt] and DI=[bpb_heads] before the jump, and dsk_boot_from_x takes them when they are sane (spt 1..63, heads 1..255), falling back to AH=08h otherwise so an old VBR chaining a new KERNEL.SYS still boots. Write the handoff (DL, BX:CX, SI, DI, BP) into SPEC 52.10.3. boothd has 7 bytes free, so this needs boot-6's -9 first.
findings.verify_note: Read both: boothd has no AH=08h ('AND NO int 13h AH=08h AT ALL'); dsk_boot_from_x.hard calls AH=08h into dsk_bootspt/dsk_boothds; dsk_bpb_check copies them into disk_spt/disk_heads for the BPB-fetching read. The stale 'same question boothd asks' comment is added to doc_fixes.

findings.title: boothd's RAM check asks the question SPEC 2.7.1 retired, and never asks about the blob
findings.detail: boothd subtracts RELOC_ADJ first, then compares the relocated segment BASE against KERNEL_SEG + ksecs*32 + BOOT_STACK/16. That is the shape boot.asm itself calls out as demanding 31,744 bytes of headroom nothing uses. It never considers the blob, which it reads to BLOB_SEG, above the image by the FAT window, .lowbss and .vgabuf. Today the over-strictness happens to cover the blob, but nothing asserts it. The built sector has 7 bytes free, not the 23 or 25 its comments claim.
evidence: build/boothd.bin: last non-zero byte at 496 of 504
findings.recommendation: Do what stage 1 does: cmp ax, MEMNEED against the top of RAM before the sub, with MEMNEED = max(BLOB_SEG + BOOT2_SECS*32 + 160, RELOC_ADJ) computed at assembly time. That drops the [ksecs] load and shift.
findings.verify_note: Code and the 7-free-byte count confirmed (boot_drive db 0x80 at 496, kofs at 504). Severity lowered medium -> low: it refuses only machines ~31KB short of what is needed, and a hard-disk machine is in practice a 640KB one; its value is the 9 bytes boot-5 needs.

findings.title: Stage 2's copy of the DPT patch is dead code in a blob with 4 bytes free
findings.detail: Stage 1 patches int 1Eh before its first multi-sector read (SPEC 2.9.8), and its own comment calls stage 2's copy 'idempotent rather than necessary'. Nothing enters boot2_entry except stage 1: FLAT_PAYLOAD jumps straight to KERNEL_SEG, the hard disk never enters stage 2, and the ROM kernel still boots through the floppy stage 1. kmain_o's dsk_dpt_init_x covers the hard-disk boot. kern_big's blob ends at 0x19FC of 0x1A00.
findings.recommendation: Delete the block, leaving stage 1's %ifndef DPT_ROM as the one site. This is the room boot-2 and boot-5 need.
findings.verify_note: Only reference to boot2_entry from outside boot2.asm is kernel.asm's jmp at .boot2 offset 0; stage 1 and stage 2 share the same DPT_ROM knob and the same SPT. Byte count re-summed from the encodings: 41.

findings.title: .bss arrives zeroed by the load, while many comments and SPEC passages say it does not
findings.detail: In the shipped kern_big, the file bytes between kernel_text_end (file 0xB788) and the next section (.ovl at 0xCE00) are all zero, and .bss (memory 0x9D88-0xB27E) maps entirely into that gap; kern_small likewise (.bss ends 0x80CB, .ovl at memory 0x8200). Every loader writes it: stage 2, boothd and kz_expand. kmain_o relies on this ('NO loader_init ... .bss is zero at boot'). mod_fp's, cpudet's, bootprof's and spl_fp's comments say '-f bin zeroes nothing', and so do a dozen more in assoc, clock, ctrl, desk and disk and several SPEC passages, while SPEC elsewhere says '.bss arrives zeroed'. The property holds by construction (the next file section starts at a memory address above .bss), but nothing asserts it.
findings.recommendation: Add one %if beside the section-end guards: the first file section after .text must start at or past BOOT2_PAD + KTEXT_SIZE + KBSS_SIZE, with an error message naming kmain_o's reliance. Then correct the comments tree-wide in one pass. Do not move data on the strength of it: .bss is as resident as .text.
findings.verify_note: Zero gap checked on build/kernel.bin; .bss and .ovl ranges checked in both maps. The contradiction is wider than three comments (grep finds ~15 in kernel/ and several in SPEC); only the three the reviewer named are in doc_fixes.

findings.title: The three hand-set constants carry their history in comments, and the history is now wrong about the present
findings.detail: The BOOT2_SECS block (kernel.asm 1983-2138) still argues for 18, 19 and 22 sectors and says kern_small is nine. The KSIG_OFF block (boot2.asm 51-115) gives eight past values and a band of 21, 57, 106..110 that boot-1 shows is wrong. The SPL_RESIDENT block (splash.inc 36-75) records three raises, none of them current. Each block opens by telling the reader to read the constant rather than the prose, then quotes numbers anyway.
findings.recommendation: For a derived or hand-set constant, the comment should state the INVARIANT and the guard that enforces it, nothing more. Move the ledger of past values to docs/history once, as KERN-BUDGET-LEDGER.md already does for the budgets.
findings.verify_note: Read all three blocks; the stale kern_small-nine paragraph and the 18/19/22 argument are in doc_fixes.

findings.title: Let the build CHOOSE KSIG_OFF and SPL_RESIDENT instead of checking hand-typed values afterwards
findings.detail: KSIG_OFF is typed twice and checked by a model; SPL_RESIDENT is typed once and sed-ed out by the Makefile. Both have moved half a dozen times, each by manual re-derivation, and boot-1 is what one wrong model costs.
findings.recommendation: Have one host tool (t_canary's crosses() with the start fixed) compute the band from the shipped geometries and emit -DKSIG_OFF=<lowest legal>. KSIG_OFF only reaches a mov si,imm16 in .boot2 and the Makefile's KSIGDEF2, so .text cannot move with it. Derive SPL_RESIDENT as in boot-4. Keep t_canary as the independent second reader.
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked: KSIG_OFF's only code use is boot2.asm's mov si, KSIG_OFF (and the KZIP %if); the Makefile adjusts it per BOOT2_XSEC/KERN_SMALL by hand.

findings.title: sch_isr draws a 28.7 ms spinner frame with IF=0 throughout kmain_o
findings.detail: From sched_init to spl_finish, every phase change (about every 220 ms) runs spl_anim inside IRQ0 without sti. That is deliberate, to avoid re-entering the scheduler, but it blocks IRQ6 (floppy completions during the boot mount and driver loads) and IRQ4 (the mouse; spl_quiet covers only the identify window) for up to 28.7 ms at a time.
findings.recommendation: Let sch_isr only set a 'frame due' byte, and draw the frame on the main line from spl_step/spl_stepq, which already hold the lock. Measure with os88boot.py phase times first.
findings.verify_note: sched.inc's own comment states the IF=0 asymmetry as deliberate; the cost is as described.

findings.title: A floppy image written to a USB stick boots drive A
findings.detail: boot.asm forces any DL above 3 to 0. A user who dd's os8088.img (instead of the live image) to a stick that the BIOS boots as USB-HDD (DL 80h) reads drive A: they get Disk error, or a kernel off whatever floppy is in A.
findings.recommendation: No code change (the sector's CHS geometry is wrong for a stick anyway). Say it in docs/LIVE-MEDIA.md's troubleshooting.
findings.verify_note: cmp dl,3 / jbe / xor dl,dl read at boot.asm 293-297.

findings.title: The floppy handoff leaves BX:CX as residue, while two comments promise zeros
findings.detail: After a canary pass BX:CX are 0. On the .nocross path (every 286 boot, every TRACKRUN build) BX holds the boot tick from [b2_t0] and CX read_run's residue, and under KZIP kz_all leaves BX holding a segment. kmain_o's and dsk_boot_from_x's comments say 'both 0'. It is harmless today, because the floppy arm ignores them.
findings.recommendation: Correct both comments and document the handoff once (boot-5). Do not spend blob bytes zeroing the registers.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed; detail sharpened (BX = the boot tick on the .nocross path). Both comments are in doc_fixes.

findings.title: Stage 1's runtime DMA-page bound for the blob read is an assembly-time fact
findings.detail: The destination is HEAP_PARA, an immediate, and the geometry is fixed per image, so whether the blob read crosses a 64KB page is known when the sector is assembled. The comment justifying the runtime code still describes the retired top-of-RAM landing.
findings.recommendation: Only if stage 1 needs the room (35 bytes free today): replace the runtime bound with a %if refusal on the kernel arm, keeping the runtime form for FLAT_PAYLOAD. Fix the comment either way.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed; free space corrected to 35 bytes (the 'Loader checksum' NUL is at 473, BS_CYLASK at 509). Comment fix is in doc_fixes.

findings.title: Shut Down uses a bare cli/sti pair and leaves hard-disk heads over data
findings.detail: The bare cli ... sti pair breaks the pushf/cli/popf rule. It is a terminal path that wants IF=1 afterwards, so it is not wrong, but nothing says so. 'You can now turn off your computer' on an XT with an ST-225 leaves the heads parked over data; period practice was PARK.COM.
findings.recommendation: Add a comment on the pair. Record head parking as a possible HDD.DRV verb (seek to the last cylinder with AH=0Ch) for Shut Down to call when a hard disk is mounted; it would live in the module, never resident.
findings.verify_note: cli at 24, sti at 54, the message at 328.

findings.title: Stage 2 could walk the FAT, which would remove 'KERNEL.SYS first and contiguous'
findings.detail: Both loaders read KERNEL.SYS as a flat run. That forces os88disk.py and the installer to place it first and contiguous, and forced the kofs patch site for non-destructive installs.
findings.recommendation: Record only. A FAT12 walker in stage 2 is ~100 blob bytes, which kern_big does not have; revisit if non-destructive installs keep failing to find a free run.
findings.prior_art: MS-DOS 5+: the boot sector loads only IO.SYS's first 3 sectors, and that loader walks the FAT for the rest, which is what let SYS stop needing IO.SYS at cluster 2.

findings.title: Make kmain_o a table rather than a call sequence
findings.detail: About 35 init calls of three kinds (OVLCALL, BLOBCALL, far shims) are interleaved with 31 hand-numbered MARKW and 8 BPMARKW sites, whose numbers may not be renumbered.
findings.recommendation: Use a blob-resident table of (kind byte, offset word) entries walked by one loop, with MARK/BPMARK emitted from the entry index; conditional calls become conditional table rows. Measure first: the win is mainly in the knob builds and in readability.
findings.prior_art: AmigaOS Kickstart RomTags (priority and flags, walked by InitCode); OS/2 CONFIG.SYS and Windows 3.x SYSTEM.INI [boot] for the declarative later half of boot.
findings.verify_note: Design suggestion; byte estimate not re-derived (kmain_o mixes OVBCALL/OVSCALL/BLOBCALL/OVLCALL/far shims, so a table needs more than three kinds).

findings.title: Guard 5 omits BLOB_LIFT on every shipped kernel
findings.detail: Guard 5 sums KERNEL_SEG*16 + KERN_SIZE + BOOT2_PAD, but on a ROM_COLD build the blob sits at HEAP_SEG + BLOB_LIFT, 1,536 bytes higher. ROM_COLD is NOT a knob: kernel.asm defines it unless NO_ROM_COLD, so kern_big and kern_small (both held to guard 5's 128KB line) carry the lift, and the guard under-counts their boot footprint by 1,536 bytes. Stage 1's own runtime check uses the lifted HEAP_PARA, so a machine is never mis-accepted; what is wrong is the build-time answer.
findings.recommendation: Use BLOB_SEG_AT in the sum so the guard and stage 1 agree by construction.
findings.verify_note: The reviewer's premise 'every ROM_COLD build is currently a knob build (exempt)' is wrong: ROM_COLD is the default on every shipped kernel, so the omission is live on kern_big and kern_small. Phase record -> now. Still low: stage 1 refuses correctly at run time and tests/small128.py boots the 128KB machine.

findings.title: boot.asm's default constants would build a wrong sector silently
findings.detail: KERNEL_SECTORS defaults to 16 and BOOT2_SECS to 2 ('must match kernel/kernel.asm's own constant'), but the real value has been 11-14 for a long time. HEAP_PARA has no default and fails loudly; these two would not.
findings.recommendation: Replace both defaults with %error on the kernel (non-FLAT_PAYLOAD) arm.
findings.verify_note: Defaults read at boot.asm 49-54; the comment is corrected in doc_fixes (comment only).

doc_fixes.old_text:
; every task, SS = LOW_SEG, ES scratch. EVERY inter-module call inside the
; kernel is near - there is no far code and no second code segment. The
; module contracts
doc_fixes.new_text:
; every task, SS = LOW_SEG, ES scratch. Calls inside `.text` are near; `.cold`
; (COLD_SEG), the boot blob ([spl_fseg]) and the boot overlay's window half
; (`.ovl`, FAT_SEG) are segments of their own, reached by far calls through
; fixed shims (SPEC.md 2.5, 2.6, 33). The module contracts
doc_fixes.why: kmain calls COLD_SEG:mem_unblob_x and kmain_o runs via OVLCALL/SPLGATE1 far calls; .cold, .boot2 and .ovl are separate segments

doc_fixes.old_text:
;   0060:0008  boot splash tick (SPEC.md 15): far-called by the boot sector
;              after every sector it reads, while the rest of this image is
;              still coming off the floppy
doc_fixes.new_text:
;   0060:0004  boot_cylrun - the loader's head-crossing finding (18.93.1);
;              0060:0008..000B are free (stage 2 calls the splash NEAR,

doc_fixes.old_text:
**Boot splash entry — 0800:0008.** A third fixed entry point sits between
the cold entry and the API table: a `jmp near spl_tick` at offset 0x0008,
**far-called by the boot sector after every sector it reads** once at least
`SPL_RESIDENT` (= 6) sectors are in memory. Contract: AX = sectors loaded
so far, DX = total sectors to load; `spl_tick` preserves every register and
segment (flags clobbered), runs on the boot stack with the boot sector's
segments, and returns with `retf`. The boot sector defines the same
`SPL_RESIDENT` constant; the two must agree with this section.
doc_fixes.new_text:
**The splash is stage 2's (§2.9.4).** There is no fixed splash entry any
more (0x0008..0x000B are free): stage 2 calls `spl_tick` **near**, after every
run it reads, once at least `SPL_RESIDENT` (= 9) sectors of `.text` are in
memory. Contract: AX = sectors loaded so far, DX = total sectors to load;
